entry.title: On the gauge-invariant orbital angular momentum of vector optical vortices in the paraxial approximation and beyond
entry.summary:
In this paper we present a gauge-invariant formalism for describing the spin and orbital angular momenta of scalar and vector optical vortices. The correction term, arising from consistent incorporation of the transverse vector potential's nonlocality, restores gauge invariance and makes it possible to separate the total angular momentum into spin and orbital components. We propose a method for calculating the orbital and spin angular momenta of multimode vector vortex fields and show that the orbital angular momentum of such beams contains two qualitatively different components.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #optics-photonics #inference

entry.title: The challenge of recognition in large scientific collaborations
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03511-0 The authorship practices of large collaborations can hide individual contributions. A recognition programme developed by the LIGO Scientific Collaboration publicly documents verified contributions to research, infrastructure and community service.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics

entry.title: Thermodynamic demonstration of tetracriticality and multicomponent superconductivity in UTe 2
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03504-z Prior measurements of the phase diagram of UTe2 contain a triple point that is forbidden by thermodynamics. Now, an additional phase boundary is discovered that resolves this problem and confirms multicomponent superconductivity in this material.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics #condensed-matter

entry.title: Multiparticle quantum walks in a dipole-conserving Bose–Hubbard model
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03512-z Strong potential gradients can localize individual particles, but interactions can still generate collective motion. An experiment with ultracold atoms in a tilted lattice now shows this collective motion by tracking mobile bound states of fractons.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics #post-quantum

entry.title: Automated inverse design of metainterfaces with tailored friction laws
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03503-0 Understanding friction between contacting surfaces is important to improve device performance. Now a method is shown to discover materials that offer on-demand frictional behaviour using inverse design based on genetic algorithms.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics

entry.title: Motors use biased diffusion to shepherd diffusible proteins on microtubules
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03489-9 Microtubules are bound by active motors and passively diffusing proteins. Now it is shown that this mixture of active and passive molecules is a realization of rectified Brownian motion in active matter.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics #genomics-proteins #clean-tech
